name: Pipedrive
tagline: Manage contacts and deals through a visual pipeline with activities and reminders

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month
pricing.notes: Official Essential monthly seat price; annual billing is lower.

tiers.name: Lite
tiers.limits: 2,500 leads+deals per paid seat (company cap 300,000), 30 custom fields, 15 reports/user, 0 automations; contacts unlimited
tiers.notes: Annual charge is $168/seat/year; current month-to-month USD amount was not exposed in the official page text checked.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: 5,000 leads+deals/seat (company cap 300,000), 100 custom fields, 50 reports/user, 50 automations/company, 5 sequences
tiers.notes: Annual charge is $468/seat/year; current month-to-month USD amount was not exposed in the official page text checked.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: 15,000 leads+deals/seat (company cap 300,000), 300 custom fields, 250 reports/user, 150 automations/company, 100 enrichment credits
tiers.notes: Annual charge is $708/seat/year; current month-to-month USD amount was not exposed in the official page text checked.

tiers.name: Ultimate
tiers.limits: 20,000 leads+deals/seat (company cap 300,000), 500 custom fields, 500 reports/user, 250 automations/company, 500 enrichment credits
tiers.notes: Annual charge is $948/seat/year; current month-to-month USD amount was not exposed in the official page text checked.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (14-day free trial; no credit card required)
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual page says save up to 42%); verified annual USD rates above, monthly USD rates not exposed in retrievable official text
pricing.hiddenCosts: Company-level add-ons are extra: LeadBooster from $32.50/month, Projects $6.67, Campaigns $13.33, Web Visitors $41 and Smart Docs $32.50 on annual billing; some are included only on higher plans. Lead/deal limits scale per seat but stop at a 300,000-company cap.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Pipedrive, manage contacts and deals through a visual pipeline with activities and reminders. The hard boundary is email sync, automations, marketplace, reporting, mobile apps, and sales workflow polish, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts and companies, move deals through a visual pipeline with activities and reminders, log interactions, and surface the next action.
whatYouLose: email sync, automations, marketplace, reporting, mobile apps, and sales workflow polish
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Pipedrive because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL; uploaded files on the application server
facts.gapVsPaid: It is less polished and less sales-focused than Pipedrive in onboarding, mobile use and turnkey automation, while also making you operate the server.
facts.setupBlocker: A server with PHP and a supported database, or Docker; production also needs HTTPS, mail, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: Frappe Cloud signup, or easy-install script, Bench or Docker
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in the Frappe site database; attachments in the site's file storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its reporting, automation and integration ecosystem is less mature than Pipedrive's, and self-hosting adds real operational work.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting means Linux plus Frappe Bench or Docker, database and Redis services, a domain, mail configuration and upgrades

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.dataFormat: Records and files live in HubSpot's cloud; CRM records can be exported as CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan gates meaningful sales automation and reporting, and the workspace is less relentlessly centered on a visual deal pipeline than Pipedrive.

alternatives.name: Krayin CRM
alternatives.desc: A Laravel sales pipeline with leads, contacts and email; glossy enough, but it still wants a PHP stack.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL; uploaded files in Laravel application storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It has a much smaller integration, mobile and reporting ecosystem than Pipedrive and leaves deployment and maintenance to you.
facts.setupBlocker: A PHP, Laravel and MySQL server stack or Docker, followed by web-server, mail, HTTPS and backup configuration

alternatives.name: Odoo Community
alternatives.desc: A free CRM buried inside an ERP the size of a small country; excellent if you can ignore the rest.

facts.install: Official Linux package, Docker image or source installation
facts.dataFormat: Business records in PostgreSQL; attachments in Odoo's filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: You trade Pipedrive's focused, quick sales workflow for the complexity and administration of a full ERP.
facts.setupBlocker: PostgreSQL, Python add-on administration and a comparatively large ERP deployment

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.dataFormat: CRM data in PostgreSQL, jobs and cache in Redis, and files in local or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is younger and less mature in mobile use, reporting, automation and integrations than Pipedrive, with self-hosting chores if you avoid the cloud plan.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker Compose, environment variables, a domain, email, persistent storage, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM Free
alternatives.desc: A full little CRM for three users and 5,000 records; the wider Zoho maze is optional.

facts.dataFormat: Records and attachments live in Zoho's cloud; record imports and exports use CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Its free tier is less fluid as a visual sales pipeline and keeps stronger automation, analytics and customization behind paid plans.

alternatives.name: Freshsales Free
alternatives.desc: A clean three-user pipeline with email and mobile apps; useful automation starts asking for rent.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records and files live in Freshworks' cloud; contacts and deals can be imported or exported by CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Advanced workflows, sequences, reporting and broader pipeline controls are paid, so the free product runs out of road sooner than Pipedrive.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Essential plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Pipedrive in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts and companies, move deals through a visual pipeline with activities and reminders, log interactions, and surface the next action.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
